repo.description:
### Summary 

OpenBao's identity templating allows SSH administrators to create roles which have variable scope based on the user's token metadata. This metadata is from an external system is not validated or constrained by OpenBao. As set by precedence of GHSA-59w7-v8rr-pr4p / CVE-2026-71543, downstream effects of this templating are within scope. Due to OpenSSH treating wildcards (`*`) as special characters to match one or more host, OpenBao administrators may inadvertently have allowed issuance of SSH certificates applying to more than one host or user. This introduces the `allow_wildcards_in_identity_templates` (defaulting to `false`) parameter to control issuance of such certificates. 

In most cases, exploiting this requires compromising an IDP, which is outside of the scope of OpenBao's threat model. 

This vulnerability is original to HashiCorp Vault. 

### Patches

This is patched in OpenBao v2.7.2. A special v2.6.5 release has been cut but note that v2.6.x series is officially unsupported upstream; please migrate to the v2.7.x series.
repo.summary: OpenBao SSH secrets engine allows wildcard '*' in host cert principals via identity templates
